name: lake
desc: A gentle young man in his late twenties: the village lamplighter. Tousled wavy brown hair, soft warm brown eyes, a warm boyish friendly face, a calm kind manner. He wears a mid-thigh-length charcoal dark-grey HOODED COAT (hood down at the back of the neck) worn OPEN down the front with no belt, its two front edges hanging straight down flat and close against his sides. It has proper set-in SLEEVES on both arms ending at the wrists. A small brass flame-shaped clasp at the throat. The open coat shows a white band-collar shirt and, over it, a fitted BURNT-ORANGE EMBER-COLOURED vest with cord X-lacing down the front. Brown pants, brown boots. No chest strap, no bag, nothing held in either hand. No part of the garment flares or stands out into empty space.
sheetHint: same face, tousled wavy brown hair, warm boyish late-twenties face, open charcoal hooded coat with proper sleeves on both arms hanging straight and close at his sides, brass flame-shaped clasp at the throat, white band-collar shirt and a burnt-orange ember-coloured X-laced vest beneath, brown pants, brown boots, no chest strap, hands empty

expressions.happy: a bright open smile, eyes lit up
expressions.worried: brows knit, small anxious frown, eyes glancing aside
expressions.determined: firm set jaw, focused eyes, faint confident smirk
expressions.tender: soft eyes, small warm smile, head fractionally tilted — the look of giving someone their name back

turnaround.extraNote: THE GARMENT IS A COAT, NOT A CAPE, and that is a MODELLING requirement rather than a style preference (2026-08-02, measured — see _capeVerdict). Sleeves are set-in on both arms so the arms bind to the ARM joints. The coat is worn OPEN (user pick 2026-08-02) and its two front edges must hang STRAIGHT DOWN close against his sides — an open coat's front panels flank the torso right beside the arms, which is the cape's failure geometry at half scale, and the only thing keeping them binding to the spine is staying within a fold's thickness of the body. If char_intake reports those panels arm-weighted, the fallback is to belt the coat closed (art kept at turnaround-cape-retired/front-belted-superseded.png).

_capeVerdict: 2026-08-02, tools/char_intake.py on the first Tripo delivery. The swept-back cape FAILED to bind: cape panel A 85.9% arm-weighted, panel B 67.1% arm / 27.7% leg, at 7,714 and 6,789 verts (the largest sheet region on any shipped model is Vesper's collar at 1,610). Cause: an auto-rigger binds each vertex to the NEAREST joint, and the cape hung ~35 cm clear of the body, where nothing near it is the spine — under a stride it scissored with the limbs. The swept-back decision itself was VINDICATED in the same pass (arms separate closed loops at 42-52%, same as Finn; both hands 100% clean), so the fix is narrower than a redesign: keep the pose, keep the hood and the charcoal silhouette, close the garment against the body. All five shipped bodies wear coats and all five bind acceptably. Retired art: public/assets/characters/lake/turnaround-cape-retired/. NOTE, superseding an earlier line in this file: while the cape survived as a garment, the cut-ins deliberately drew it draped FORWARD (dramatic chest-up) while the turnaround swept it back (bindable) — one garment, two drapes, which is legitimate because a portrait never animates. That reasoning DIED with the cape. Lake now owns no cape at all, so a cape in a portrait is a plain continuity error and the cut-ins must be re-rolled to the open coat, not merely recoloured.
_lookNote: Identity ratified 2026-08-02 from public/assets/refs/lake.jpeg (user pick: base candidate 3). OPEN coat + BURNT-ORANGE EMBER vest are the user's 2026-08-02 picks: they chose the open-front silhouette on look, and asked for a flame colour in place of the green (three temperatures were rendered — ember-orange, rust-red, flame-scarlet; ember-orange chosen because it sits inside the golden-hour town palette where scarlet fights it, and because it is lamp-glow rather than fire. Scarlet's counter-argument, kept on record: it reads better at the town's 65 px character height).
_chainNote: THE WHOLE CHAIN HANGS OFF turnaround/front.png, and that ordering is load-bearing (2026-08-02). Two measured failure modes it exists to dodge: (1) PROSE CANNOT PIN A STYLE. Rolls conditioned on bust.png drifted to semi-photoreal ~7-head adults 4 times in 5; rolls chained off an already-on-model A-pose held style AND identity 6 times in 6. gen-character.mjs's normal chain starts at a TEXT-ONLY `key`, so it was bypassed here on purpose — regenerating this face from prose returns a plausible stranger. (2) THE REFERENCE IMAGE DICTATES THE CROP, PROSE DOES NOT REACH IT. Asking for a 'half-body bust' while passing a full-body A-pose returned a full-body render; passing a chest-up CROP of that same A-pose returned the bust. Same finding the cut-in pipeline measured independently. So: front A-pose -> cropped -> bust-key -> bust, and left/right/back chained off the front. Known slip, accepted under the prototype bar: the two profile views draw buttons down the coat's front edge that the front view has no trace of.
